title: fix(devx): read a regex literal as a literal in the shared textual scanners
body: Fixes #14742 `skipStringLiteral` — the one literal-skipper `scanTopLevel`, `enclosingOpeners`, `sliceBalanced` and `splitTopLevel` share — opened a string on any `'`, `"` or backtick. A **regex literal** whose character class carries one of those three opened a literal the source does not have, and every byte after it in the file was read with the string/code polarity reversed. The live instance is in `packages/rest/src/error-response.ts`: ```ts const RELATION_DOES_NOT_EXIST = /\brelation\s+["'`][^"'`]+["'`]\s+does not exist/i; ``` ## The rule, from the grammar rather than approximated ECMA-262's lexical grammar has two goal symbols, `InputElementDiv` and `InputElementRegExp`, and the syntactic grammar decides which applies: a `/` opens a `RegularExpressionLiteral` only where an expression may begin. The recogniser (`regexMayBeginAt` / `regexLiteralAt`) implements the productions directly, and three of their consequences are load-bearing here rather than incidental: - `RegularExpressionFirstChar` excludes `*` and `/`, which is the grammar's own reason `//` and `/*` are comments and never a regex — not a special case bolted on; - a `RegularExpressionClass` is where `/`, `'`, `"` and `` ` `` are **ordinary characters** — this card's whole defect; - `RegularExpressionNonTerminator` excludes a LineTerminator, so a `/` whose body does not close on its line was a division. ### The three positions the preceding character cannot decide ⛔ Not approximated, and not resolved in the convenient direction. Reading a `/` as a regex **skips a span**; if the `/` was division, that span is a literal the source does not contain — this card's own defect in a new spelling, and an uncounted one. So each undecidable case is classified as **division**, which skips nothing and can only leave a regex unread (the status quo, already counted), never invent one: | position | division | regex | read as | |:--|:--|:--|:--| | after `)` | `(a + b) / 2` | `if (x) /re/.test(y)` | division | | after `}` | `{ a: 1 } / 2` | `if (x) { f() }` then `/re/.test(y)` | division | | after a bare `<` / `>` | `a > b / c`, and `.tsx` JSX `` | `a > /re/.test(s)` | division | `=>` and `>=`/`<=` are **not** this case: the character before the `>` decides them, and both are expression positions. This is not an AST. The recogniser reads one character backwards and matches one production forwards; the file's "Why textual, not AST" note stands unchanged. ## Measured against an independent parser, both directions A scanner cannot certify its own literal spans, so the residue is diffed against the TypeScript compiler's own parse (typescript 6.0.3), which carries the real goal state. Every `/` the language calls code, over the same population: | | | |:--|--:| | `/` bytes in code position | 1615 | | agreed to be regex literals (closing `/` included) | 1496 | | ⭐⭐ **fabricated** — division read as a regex | **0** | | ⭐ **missed** — a real regex read as division | **0** | | closing-slash mismatches | 0 | | undecidable positions read as division | 47 | | …of which after `)` / after `}` / after a bare `<` | 45 / 0 / 2 | | ⭐ …of which the compiler says were regex literals | **0** | All 45 `)` cases are arithmetic; both `<` cases are JSX closing tags in `packages/client-react/src/context.tsx`. So the conservative classification costs **nothing measured** on this tree and prevents two concrete fabrications. ## Ledgers re-derived by MEASUREMENT Both ends measured on today's tree — the pre-fix Both readings carry the instrument check the census was built with: with its fallback OFF the replica reproduces the real `deriveSites` `objlithelper` output exactly (29 sites, 5 unresolved) on the pre-fix and post-fix primitives alike. ## ⭐⭐ The row that decides it: no registration is owed `deriveSites` output diffed **key by key** across the change, over the same population, exactly as #14626 did: **63 sites, 5 unresolved, before and after, and the diff is empty in both directions.** The card's "unregistered wire codes hiding behind it today: not knowable without closing it" row therefore resolves to **0** — there is no separate registration decision to escalate, and nothing in this PR registers anything. ## The pin that reds by design The `--self-test` case asserted the **opposite** direction — a regex fixture had to come back `desync` — and its own message said to re-measure rather than edit it. It red on the first run, exactly as the card predicted. The **fixture is unchanged**; only the expected answer moved (`desync` → `bracket`), which is what keeps the two readings comparable, and its message now says what to do if the class ever re-opens. A new battery pins the recogniser in both directions (39 cases): the live instance and each of the four primitives that inherit it; `a / b / c`, `x = y / 2 / z`, `(a) / b`, `arr[0] / n`, `map.delete / 2` and `i++ / 2` as negative fixtures; the grammar's comment and line-terminator exclusions; the `return`/arrow keyword positions; the three undecidable positions pinned **as division**; and the sibling recogniser in `scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs` — both where the two are supposed to agree and at the one place they deliberately differ (after `}` the masker says regex, which is right for a masker that fails safe by over-masking, and wrong for a scanner that must never skip a span it invented). ## Verification — every verdict line, exit code captured before any pipe All run on the final commit `62bec1012`. ``` node scripts/check-dispatcher-error-vocabulary.mjs --self-test EXIT=0 check-dispatcher-error-vocabulary --self-test: 10 shapes + 322 assertions OK (vocabulary + #9098 door typing) (pre-fix, same tree: 282 assertions OK — +40 cases, no case removed) node scripts/check-dispatcher-error-vocabulary.mjs EXIT=0 check-dispatcher-error-vocabulary: OK — 63 unregistered code-stamping site(s), all classified; 2 awaiting a ledger entry (#8846). No command reported exit 3, `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` or `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, so none is recorded as NOT MEASURED. ⚠️ The derivation printed a STALE TREE notice: this branch is cut at `0db29473c` and `origin/main` has since moved to `e8c7956c4`, across which `scripts/measure-self-test-floor.mjs` changed.
